choices.content: A number whose absolute value equals itself is positive.
Two additive inverses have equal absolute values.
The absolute value of any number is greater than \(0\).
The number with the smallest absolute value is \(-1\).

question.prompt: Which of the following statements is correct?

solutions.explanation: Two additive inverses are the same distance from the origin, so their absolute values are equal. Numbers whose absolute values equal themselves are nonnegative (including \(0\)); the absolute value of \(0\) is \(0\); the number with the smallest absolute value is \(0\).
solutions.title: Absolute-value properties and zero
